# Merged PRs read red from the mergeability controller's post-merge runs

## Context

Operator, 2026-10-23: PRs merge only at fully green CI, yet the merged-PR list shows most of them red, which reads to an outside evaluator as a team merging broken PRs. Measured on the 30 most recently merged `neomjs/neo` PRs at 13:4xZ (`statusCheckRollup` of each PR's last head commit, the field the list icon renders):

| | PRs |
|---|---|
| rollup `FAILURE` | 19 of 30 |
| of those, red **only** from runs that started after `mergedAt` | 12 |
| still red without the controller's items (superseded same-head runs, below) | 7 |

The 60 red contexts across those 19 heads, by source:

| red context | count | started |
|---|---|---|
| `Review Admission Mergeability` matrix job `PR (N)`, `CANCELLED` | 28 | after merge |
| `Review Admission Mergeability` matrix job `PR (N)`, `FAILURE` | 13 | after merge |
| commit status `review-admission/mergeability` = `error` | 11 | after merge |
| `File Size Guard / check-size`, `CANCELLED` | 6 | before merge |
| `PR Baseline / baseline / PR body`, `FAILURE` | 2 | before merge |

Receipts: run 39960822280 (`pull_request_target`, created 13:23:40Z, three seconds after #20055 merged at 13:23:37Z) is anchored on #20055's head `2989e393c4` and spawned `PR (19958)`, `PR (20024)`, `PR (20044)`, `PR (20049)`, `PR (20052)`, all five `cancelled` with zero steps run. Run 39960695212 on #20051's head `92e67a589e` (created 13:22:45Z; #20051 merged 13:22:42Z) ran job 120437832432 `PR (20055)` at 13:26:29Z, three minutes after #20055 had merged, and ended `##[error] PR #20055 mergeability stayed null after 4 bounded polls` after logging `PR #20055 already publishes review-admission/mergeability=error`: the `error` status an earlier such job had written onto #20055's merged head.

Live latest-open sweep: the newest 20 open issues read at 2026-10-23 13:48Z; no equivalent. `review-admission` across all states: #17692 (origin, closed) and #18226 (coverage restoration, closed); neither names the symptom. Memory Core rationale sweep (`query_raw_memories` on the merged-head symptom): no prior decision. A2A claims of the last hour: none on this surface. Own open assignments: none on this surface.

## The Problem

`.github/workflows/review-admission-mergeability.yml` publishes the `review-admission/mergeability` commit status onto every open dev-target PR head (#17692). Two of its paths run **after** a PR has stopped being a PR under review, and both leave red on heads that earned green:

1. **The merged-close sweep anchors on the merged head.** `pull_request_target` with `types: [..., closed]` fires on the merge; `discover` treats `closed && merged` as a board trigger and spawns one `publish` matrix job per open PR. GitHub anchors a `pull_request_target` run's check runs on the event PR's head SHA, so every `PR (N)` job of that sweep is a check run on the **merged** PR. The same merge is also a `push` to `dev`, which runs the identical sweep anchored on the new dev commit: the closed-event sweep re-evaluates nothing the push sweep does not, it only doubles the burst. The doubled jobs then collapse in the per-PR concurrency group (`cancel-in-progress: false` keeps one running and one pending; a third arrival cancels the pending one), and a cancelled job is a red check run on the merged head for good.

2. **A job whose target merged mid-sweep writes `error` onto that merged head.** `pulls.get` on a closed PR returns `mergeable: null` permanently; the bounded poll exhausts, `publish('error', …)` lands on the now-merged head, and `core.setFailed` reds the job, a second red context on whichever head anchored the run. With several approved PRs merging within a minute, the board sweep of merge 1 regularly targets the PR of merge 2.

Both are cosmetic for the gate itself (`manage_pr_reviewers(add)` reads the live status of **open** PRs) and both are permanent on the merged head, because check runs and the latest status per context on a SHA are what the list icon rolls up.

**Superseded same-head runs (the residual 7 of 30), out of this ticket's scope but named:** a workflow re-triggered on an unchanged head by a body edit (`pull_request: edited`) leaves its first run's conclusion on that head beside the later green one; GitHub's rollup counts every check run, not the latest per name (#20032: two cancelled `check-size` runs at 07:17Z and 07:20Z, three green ones later on the same head, rollup `FAILURE`). `File Size Guard` cancels the in-progress same-head run under `cancel-in-progress: true` (6); `PR Baseline / PR body` failed once on an earlier body revision and passed on the next (2). That class is #20064.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.github/workflows/review-admission-mergeability.yml:6-8`: `pull_request_target` types include `closed`; `:11-12`: `push: branches: [dev]` fires on the same merge; `:15-17`: `workflow_run` on Data Sync covers the `[skip ci]` commits. The header comments (`:4-5`, `:9-10`) state the trigger rationale: head movement evaluates one PR, base movement sweeps the board.
- `:41-61`: `discover` branches on `isClosed` / `isMergedClose`: merged close → board sweep; unmerged close → `prs = []` (a no-op run that still anchors a green check run on the closed head).
- `:153-158`: per-PR `concurrency` group with `cancel-in-progress: false`, the serialization that makes a burst's pending jobs cancel.
- `:178-182`: `readPull` returns the PR without reading `state`; `:248-250`, `:268-270`: `mergeable === null` continues the poll; `:297-298`: exhaustion publishes `error` and fails the job; `:304-313`: any thrown error also publishes `error` on `lastCoordinate`.
- GitHub anchors `pull_request_target` check runs on the PR head (run 39960822280, event `pull_request_target`, is listed by `gh run list --commit 2989e393c4`, #20055's head, created 13:23:40Z) and `push` check runs on the pushed commit; commit statuses are per SHA + context with latest-write-wins; the PR list icon renders the head commit's `statusCheckRollup.state`, in which any `CANCELLED` / `FAILURE` / `ERROR` context makes the state `FAILURE`.
- No unit arm at `dev` d0f92ff6a6 evaluates the committed controller script (`grep -ril mergeability test/` is empty; the `WorkflowConcurrency.spec.mjs` restoration #18226 names is not in the tree), so the evidence for this change is a scratch evaluation of the committed `github-script` block against mocks plus the post-merge rollup census.

Design authority: #17692's AC lists "merged-close, ordinary `dev` push, and trusted Data Sync completion" as the three board triggers. The merged-close arm's purpose (re-evaluate after a base move) is fully carried by the `push` the same merge produces; dropping the arm removes a duplicate sweep, not a re-evaluation. The `error`-on-closed-head behaviour was never specified: #17692 specifies `error` for exhausted `null` on a **live** PR coordinate, and a closed PR has no live coordinate.

## The Fix

`.github/workflows/review-admission-mergeability.yml`, nothing else:

1. **Drop `closed` from the `pull_request_target` types** and delete the `isClosed` / `isMergedClose` branches in `discover` (PR event → `[eventPr]`, everything else → board sweep). The header comment gains the one sentence that says why: the merge's own `push` sweeps the board, anchored on the dev commit.
2. **A PR observed closed gets no status and no failure.** `readPull` throws a `PullClosed` sentinel when `data.state !== 'open'`; the `catch` returns on it with `core.info` before the `error`-publish branch. The merged head keeps whatever verdict it earned while open. One window stays, inherited from #17692's API shape: `publish` awaits `getCombinedStatusForRef` after the job's last open read, so a close inside that await can still land one write on the merged head; so can the >32 overflow sweep's list-snapshot writes and the generic-error fallback. None of these is the measured class (0 of the 52 items); the AC-3 census records them if they occur (Euclid's review boundary, 14:14Z).
3. No change to the per-PR concurrency, the poll bounds, the overflow cap or the `push` / `workflow_run` / `workflow_dispatch` triggers.

About as many lines leave (the trigger type, the dead branching) as arrive (the guard).

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `review-admission/mergeability` status on a PR head | live `pulls.get` of an **open** PR (#17692) | unchanged for open PRs; a PR observed closed or merged at any of its job's reads receives **no** write and the job ends green with an info line | the next `push: dev` sweep re-evaluates every open PR as today; a close inside the status write's own await (publication window), an overflow snapshot write or the generic-error fallback can still land one write, recorded by the AC-3 census | workflow header + the `readPull` comment | AC-2 harness: closed PR → zero `createCommitStatus`, zero `setFailed`; open `null`-exhausted PR → `error` + `setFailed` as before |
| Controller triggers | GitHub event model (#17692) | `pull_request_target` on `opened` / `reopened` / `synchronize` / `ready_for_review`; board sweeps on `push: dev`, Data Sync `workflow_run`, `workflow_dispatch` | none needed: a merge is a `push` | workflow header | the YAML; AC-3 |
| Merged-PR head `statusCheckRollup` | GitHub rollup | no `Review Admission Mergeability` check run from a closed-event sweep and no `review-admission/mergeability` write by a job that observed the close lands on a head after its PR merged; publication-window, overflow and generic-error writes are the named residual | — | — | AC-3 |

## Decision Record impact

`none`: the controller keeps the #17692 shape; one duplicate trigger arm and one unspecified write path leave.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 **Trigger:** the committed `on.pull_request_target.types` is exactly `[opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review]`; `discover` has no `closed` branch; `push: dev`, `workflow_run` and `workflow_dispatch` are unchanged.
- [ ] AC-2 **Closed-PR guard, evaluated red-first:** the committed `publish` script string, run against a mocked `github` whose `pulls.get` returns `{state: 'closed', merged: true, mergeable: null, head, base}`, makes **zero** `repos.createCommitStatus` calls and **zero** `core.setFailed` calls (on `dev` today: one `error` write and one `setFailed`); the same harness with `{state: 'open', mergeable: null}` throughout still publishes `error` and fails, and `{state: 'open', mergeable: false}` still publishes `failure` (the #17692 behaviour, unchanged). All arms' output in the PR body.
- [ ] AC-3 **Post-merge only, bounded to the observed-close guard:** for the first five or more PRs merged after this change lands, (a) no `pull_request_target` run anchored on the merged head is **created** after `mergedAt` (the closed-event trigger is gone; a run queued before the close may still start after it), (b) no `Review Admission Mergeability` check run on the head concludes red (`FAILURE` / `CANCELLED`) with a start after `mergedAt`: a job that starts late and ends green on `PullClosed` is recorded, not counted, and (c) any `review-admission/mergeability` status created after `mergedAt` is a publication-window, overflow or generic-error write, recorded with its run id as the census's residual, owner #20022. Census on this ticket, with the `gh api graphql` query of the Context measurement.
- [ ] AC-4 **Gate intact:** an open PR that conflicts with `dev` after a later merge still turns `review-admission/mergeability` to `failure` on the next `push: dev` sweep (one live instance, or the AC-2 harness arm).

## Out of Scope

- The publication window (a close between the job's last open read and its status POST), the >32 overflow sweep's list-snapshot writes and the generic-error fallback: inherited from #17692's API shape (GitHub offers no atomic compare-and-write), 0 of the 52 measured items, recorded by the AC-3 census under #20022; a redesign is not for this patch.
- The superseded same-head runs (`File Size Guard` cancellations, `PR Baseline / PR body` first-revision failures): #20064.
- The `dev` commit list, where 21 of the last 30 commits roll up red mostly from `Engine Tests` / `E2E (engine tier)` push runs cancelled by the next merge (`cancel-in-progress: true` keyed on `github.ref`): a runner-budget decision, the operator's.
- The per-PR concurrency shape of the controller (after this change its cancellations land on dev commits only; 37 of the dev list's 215 red contexts today).
- Making the status a required context (#17171's domain).

## Avoided Traps

- **`continue-on-error` or a green-on-failure job:** a failed or cancelled job's check run is red in the rollup regardless of the run's conclusion.
- **Deleting the controller's `push` sweep to stop the burst:** the push sweep is the load-bearing base-move response (#17692); the closed sweep is the duplicate.
- **Keying the per-PR concurrency by run id:** removes the cancellations by letting stale writes race, the exact hazard #17692 serialized against.

## Related

#17692 (origin; PR #17696), #18226 (coverage restoration, closed, spec absent at `dev`), #20064 (the same-head rerun class), #20022 (the v13.3.1 cut; the operator's item for the patch), #17171 (required-context policy).
